title: JavaScript Advanced Async Patterns Applied Check
description: Apply advanced asynchronous patterns by choosing cancellation, retries, backoff, concurrency limits, stale-result protection, queues, debounce, throttle, async iterators, and Observables for realistic JavaScript scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: A Promise object then a Promise object

questions.explanation: Each `.next()` resumes the generator until the next `yield`.

questions.prompt: Which pattern best fits an API that returns pages of results until `hasMore` is false?

options.text: An async generator consumed with `for await...of`
A JSON string with no loop

questions.explanation: Async generators are a clean way to hide pagination and yield pages or items over time.

options.text: `console.log("done")` runs before the async saves finish
`forEach()` automatically waits for every async callback
`await` cannot be used in any callback

questions.explanation: `forEach()` does not await async callbacks. Use `for...of` for sequential work or `Promise.all()` for concurrent work.

questions.prompt: A user leaves a page while a `fetch()` request is still running. Which tool is most appropriate for cancelling the request?
questions.explanation: `AbortController` can cancel a fetch request when its signal is passed to `fetch()`.

options.text: It clears the timer whether the request succeeds, fails, or is aborted
It forces the request to return JSON

questions.explanation: `finally` is ideal for cleanup that should run after any outcome.

questions.prompt: Which response status is usually a better retry candidate?
questions.explanation: `503` is often temporary. Client errors such as `400`, `401`, and `404` usually need a different fix.

questions.prompt: What is a risk of retrying a request that creates an order?

options.text: It may create duplicate orders unless the API handles idempotency
It will always become a GET request
It prevents the server from reading JSON

questions.explanation: Retrying write operations can duplicate side effects unless the server supports safeguards such as idempotency keys.

questions.prompt: Which approach is best for uploading 100 files without starting all uploads at once?

options.text: Use a concurrency limit or queue
Use `Promise.all()` on the full list with no limit

questions.explanation: A limit or queue controls how many uploads are in progress at a time.

questions.prompt: A search for `ab` finishes before an older search for `a`. The older result then overwrites the UI. What problem is this?
questions.explanation: The older async result is stale because it no longer matches the user's latest query.

questions.prompt: Which check prevents an older request from updating the UI?

options.text: Compare the request's id to the latest request id before rendering
Convert the result to a string and ignore timing

questions.explanation: A request id lets only the latest operation update state.

questions.prompt: Which pattern best fits work that arrives over time and must be processed one task at a time?
questions.explanation: An async queue stores tasks and processes them in a controlled order.

questions.prompt: A search request should run after the user stops typing for 300ms. Which pattern should you use?
questions.explanation: Debouncing waits for a pause in frequent events.

questions.prompt: A scroll handler should run at most once every 500ms while scrolling continues. Which pattern should you use?
questions.explanation: Throttling limits a function to at most one run per time window.

options.text: It creates a new debounced function for every input event
It never passes the input value
It automatically cancels all fetch requests

questions.explanation: The debounced function should be created once and reused, otherwise each event has its own timer.

questions.prompt: When should you consider an Observable-style pattern?

options.text: When handling a push-based stream of values over time
When making one simple request for one result
When replacing every function with a class
When avoiding cleanup for long-lived events

questions.explanation: Observables fit push-based event streams such as live messages, input streams, or dashboards.
